newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt nudged higher, boosted by U.S. moves.
newsitem.headline: German debt nudged higher, boosted by U.S. moves.

text.p: German debt nudged higher in late trading on Friday, buoyed both by stronger U.S. Treasuries and hopes that European nations will be successful in hammering out differences in time for a prompt launch of currency union.
By the end of trading the September Bund futures contract traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange was up 16 basis points at 101.55, having traded in a range between 101.73 and 101.21.
Dealers were delighted by news that U.S. inflationary pressures appeared under control, raising hopes that rates would remain steady in the near term.

The U.S. Labour Department said on Friday that producer prices fell 0.3 percent in May and that the producer price index, excluding the volatile food and energy componets, was also down 0.3 percent. This marks the fifth consecutive decline and appeared to confirm there were few inflationary pressures in the pipeline.
Since economists had predicted a 0.1 percent jump in both the overall and the core index, a short squeeze helped prices rise shortly before the weekend.
Soothing comments from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl that about the prospects on EMU were also supportive.

While dealers still said the market would remain volatile in the coming days as policy makers attempt to sort out the stability pact issue at the Amsterdam summit, they were move confident again about the whole idea.
"The EMU issue will continue to be the primary topic, but things are looking a little bit better now," a dealer said.

Leaders will meet in Amsterdam on Monday and Tuesday and lower level officials are scheduled to have meetings ahead of time, sending signals that some sort of compromise might be worked out, dealers said. But dealers were unwilling to predict what might happen early next week in the market.
"That all depends on what we hear this weekend and early next week on the Euro issue," another dealer said.
